messages.content: What is the earliest reference of Jesus Christ in history from historical record?

function.name: get_earliest_reference
function.description: Retrieve the earliest historical reference of a person. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

source.description: Source to fetch the reference. Default is 'scriptures'

message.content:
**Earliest non‑Christian historical reference to Jesus Christ**

| Source | Date (approx.) | Passage | Significance |
|--------|----------------|---------|--------------|
| **Flavius Josephus – *Antiquities of the Jews*, Book 18, Chapter 3** | 93–94 CE | “Now there was a wise man named **Jesus**, who was a doer of wonderful works… He was crucified by Pontius Pilate during the reign of Tiberius.” | This is the earliest surviving mention of Jesus in a secular, contemporary text. It appears in a passage that is now widely regarded as authentic (the “Testimonium Flavianum”), though it has been subject to later Christian interpolation. Even the minimal, “Jesus was a wise man… crucified by Pilate” is considered historically reliable by most scholars. |
| **Tacitus – *Annals*, Book 15, Chapter 44** | 116 CE | “The emperor Tiberius, after he had suffered the loss of his son, had the emperor’s name… and the emperor’s name was… *Christus*… crucified by Pontius Pilate.” | Provides an independent Roman confirmation of Jesus’ execution under Pilate. It is not the earliest, but it corroborates Josephus. |
| **Pliny the Younger – *Letters*, 1.10** | 112 CE | “The Christians worship Christ as a god.” | Shows that by the early 2nd century, a cult of Christ existed in Rome. |
| **Babylonian Talmud – *Sanhedrin* 43a** | 3rd–5th century CE | “Jesus was hanged on the eve of Passover.” | A Jewish source that confirms the crucifixion, though it is later than the Roman and Josephus references. |

### Bottom line
The **earliest surviving historical record** that mentions Jesus Christ outside the New Testament is **Josephus’ *Antiquities* (93–94 CE)**. While the passage has been debated, the core statement that Jesus was a real person who was crucified by Pontius Pilate is accepted by the vast majority of historians. Subsequent references (Tacitus, Pliny, the Talmud) confirm and elaborate on this basic fact.
